guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

tone.target: huge dry modal riff with thick lower-mid crunch
tone.profile: huge dry modal riff with thick lower-mid crunch
tone.summary: A classic Marshall-style chain using the UK 45 amp model for a powerful, mid-focused crunch, paired with the UK Vintage 4x12 cab. Compression and OD boost are used to tighten the riff and enhance the lower-mid punch, while minimal reverb adds space without sounding wet.

blocks.purpose: Clean up the signal and tighten the riff edges.
Provide a solid push into the amp to maximize the crunch and punch of the riff.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Comp for maximum clean-up and drive without adding color, focusing on pure power.

blocks.purpose: Add the necessary thick crunch and sustain for the drone-like riff without sounding overly fuzzy.
blocks.gap: The 'Distortion' model provides a versatile, mid-heavy grit suitable for Zeppelin's tone.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound required for powerful British rock riffs, emphasizing mids.
Provide the classic British rock cabinet sound and necessary frequency response.
Sculpt the tone to emphasize thick lower-mids and cut out excessive low end/highs for a tighter, punchier riff.
blocks.gap: Used EQ 2 for its ability to precisely scoop frequencies around the critical mid-range area.

alternatives.reason: Also suitable, but EQ 2 offers better control over specific frequency bands.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and depth without introducing noticeable wash or ambience (minimal reverb).
blocks.gap: The requirement is 'minimal ambience,' so Room is chosen over Plate/Spring for its natural, non-metallic decay.

alternatives.reason: Could also work but might sound too bright.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more natural, vintage 4x12 that better captures the dry, thick lower-mid crunch required.

proposals.reason: Enhance the natural, dry character and lower-mid thickness of the riff tone.
